change: build_config.rb adds mruby-task (at 4.0.0-rc2 through hal-posix-task, at head through the gem itself, the port layer carrying the HAL)
why: capstone/bug-corpora/mruby/gc-slot-repros names mruby-task as the reason four of its candidates cannot be reached: the reports that carry the reused-GC-slot signature exactly (mruby #6870, #6886, #6872, #6887, 'Assertion failed: ((obj)->tt != MRB_TT_FREE), function mrb_gc_mark') all go through mrb_task_mark_all, and the gem is in none of the port's gemboxes
what_the_gem_needs: the POSIX task HAL (mrbgems/hal-posix-task/src/task_hal.c) drives its tick with sigaction(SIGALRM) plus setitimer(ITIMER_REAL), and sleeps with clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) and nanosleep. All four are delegated on #144, and none of them is a thread: that is why the gem builds for a domain now and did not before.

platform.note: the platform of the delegation-v0-removal-stack checks (#144); guest --cma-mib 1024 --process-cache-mib 768

head.per_test: one test differs from native, the same one this port's stdlib-io record reports: 'Process.kill passes the pid selectors on' crashes on Process.kill(0, 0). The launcher rule that refuses it is changed in the fd-rows runtime branch; with that launcher the same image has no crash.

4.0.0-rc2.per_test: every test's status is the native one

task_scripts: three task workloads (tasks allocating across Task.pass, a task holding a string across a yield, and a root-context Task.pass loop while background tasks run) complete in the domain with status 0 in both pins

reproduction_attempted.defect: mruby #6886, fixed upstream by 456a8687a 'gc.c: re-mark task stacks in final_marking_phase' (2026-06-12, after the pin)
reproduction_attempted.live_at_the_pin: yes, read in the pin's own source: mrb_task_mark_all is called from root_scan_phase (src/gc.c:1251-1253) and final_marking_phase (src/gc.c:1334-1356) does not call it
reproduction_attempted.ground_truth_arm: the pin's tree with mruby-task, MRB_DEBUG (so mrb_assert is live) and ASan, and WITHOUT MRB_GC_STRESS, because a full GC at every allocation closes the very window this defect needs
reproduction_attempted.workloads: three Ruby workloads written to the fix commit's own mechanism: objects allocated into task stack slots across Task.pass; the same with GC.generational_mode=false and GC.step_ratio=1 to hold the incremental window open; and old objects moved out of a container into a task slot during the mark phase
reproduction_attempted.result: none of them fires at the pin
reproduction_attempted.positive_control: an arm built with the root_scan_phase call to mrb_task_mark_all compiled out, so task stacks are never marked at all. The first workload faults there under ASan (SEGV in mrb_vm_exec at src/vm.c:2692) in three of four knob settings, so the instrument fires and that workload does put objects solely on task stacks across a collection. The other two workloads do not fault even in that arm, so they never put an object solely on a task stack and say nothing either way.
reproduction_attempted.reading: the workload reaches the gem but not the race: the defect needs a task stack slot written during the incremental mark phase with an object the root scan did not see, which a Ruby script does not place precisely. This is the conclusion the corpus already reached for the realloc-vmstack rows, and it points the same way: a C-level case that drives the collector's phases directly.
